### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **212** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **168** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json efb1620c63bd1c8fc92fdcf82c922dccfac90eed` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c6f7425ffaa563b825cac513c3d51e93e6c06649` — the merge of head `869cdd31654233e947476fb3ce7c68ecffaaadb9` into base `efb1620c63bd1c8fc92fdcf82c922dccfac90eed`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c6f7425ffaa563b825cac513c3d51e93e6c06649 && git checkout c6f7425ffaa563b825cac513c3d51e93e6c06649
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin efb1620c63bd1c8fc92fdcf82c922dccfac90eed 869cdd31654233e947476fb3ce7c68ecffaaadb9 && git checkout -B drift-repro efb1620c63bd1c8fc92fdcf82c922dccfac90eed && git merge --no-ff 869cdd31654233e947476fb3ce7c68ecffaaadb9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json efb1620c63bd1c8fc92fdcf82c922dccfac90eed
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `869cdd31654233e947476fb3ce7c68ecffaaadb9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/control-flow.zod.ts + packages/spec/src/automation/control-flow.test.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/bpmn-mapping.ts, packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/logic-nodes.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/dag-traversal.ts, packages/lint/src/lint-flow-patterns.ts, docs/adr/0031-advanced-flow-node-executors-and-dag.md, hotcrm `src/sales/flows/_guarded-iteration.ts`

Face: published schema (`packages/spec/src/**`, non-test). Inputs read: PR #28518 body and file list, card #28055 with triage `6521001083` and the dev report `6553451590`, parent #27381 (row 4), the dispatch order `order-28055.md`, the diff `origin/main...869cdd31` (merge base `1f1a369b`), the head's check-runs, and the cited code on `main`. Nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The accept set does not move.** The predicate is untouched: `analyzeRegion` still pushes exactly one error when the region has more than one exit, at the same branch, and the zero-exit, single-entry, duplicate-id, edge-integrity and cycle lines are byte-identical. `entryId` / `exitId` are derived from `entries.length === 1` / `exits.length === 1` as before, so every caller that reads the shape (`findRegionEntry`, the engine's `runRegion`, `bpmn-mapping`) sees the same verdict on the same input. `validateControlFlow` still throws `WHERE: errors.join('; ')`, so the `where` path (`try_catch 'tc' try`, `loop 'sweep' body`, `parallel 'fan' branch 1`) is unchanged. Correct.
2. **The lead is byte-identical.** `multiExitRefusal` opens with `region must be single-exit but has N: a, b`, the old sentence verbatim, then ` — ` and the cure. The pre-existing pin at `control-flow.test.ts` (`rejects multiple exit nodes`, `/single-exit/`) holds without edit. Correct.
3. **No published-surface move.** `multiExitRefusal` is a private module function; `analyzeRegion`'s signature and `RegionAnalysis` are unchanged, so `packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json` (`analyzeRegion (function)`) does not move. No `packages/spec/authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` shard is in the diff (three files: the changeset, the test, the producer). The `./automation` export map is untouched. Correct.
4. **The prescription is true for all three region kinds.** `validateControlFlow` walks every slot `regionSlotsOf` yields: `loop.config.body`, each `parallel.config.branches[i]`, `try_catch.config.try` and `.catch`; all four reach the same `analyzeRegion` line. Adding one node with an in-edge from each exit makes it the only node without an out-edge in a DAG, so the region becomes single-exit and stays acyclic and single-entry; the test `the join it prescribes is accepted` pins that at the registration door for `try_catch`, and the mechanism is slot-independent. The run-time contract (ADR-0031: the container resumes after the region's one exit; `runRegion` starts at `findRegionEntry`) is unchanged. Correct.
5. **The node kind named exists and is inert.** `assignment` is a `FlowNodeAction` (`flow.zod.ts` line 47), registered as a built-in executor (`logic-nodes.ts` line 142) whose descriptor declares no `required` ("No `required`: an empty node is valid") and whose `execute` folds `node.config ?? {}` to zero pairs. `config` is optional on `FlowNodeSchema` (`flow.zod.ts` line 631). It is the same node `@objectstack/lint`'s `MINIMAL_CATCH_REGION` hint names and the handler HotCRM's `_guarded-iteration.ts` ships. No `noop` type is named (none is registered; the `'noop'` in an existing parse-only test is a string, not an executor). Correct.
6. **Pins and restatements.** `git grep "region must be single-exit"` at the head across `packages/`, `content/docs/`, `skills/`, `ui/`, `apps/`, `examples/`: the producer, the new tests and the changeset only. `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`, `content/docs/references/automation/control-flow.mdx`, the service-automation README and node descriptors state the single-entry/single-exit rule but never quote the refusal, so they stay true. `skills/**` carries no restatement; the Governed Surface Queue Guard check-run on this head is `success`, consistent with no governed path in the file list. Correct.
7. **No consumer parses the message.** Searched `single-exit but has`, `region must be`, `must be single-` and `split('; ')` across objectstack (`packages/`, `ui/`, `apps/`, `examples/`, `skills/`, `content/`), hotcrm and objectui: no match on this refusal. The two `split('; ')` sites found (`packages/rest` and `ui/packages/app-shell` tests) read unrelated messages. The `bpmn-mapping` wrapper (`region is not single-entry/single-exit — errors.join('; ')`) and `findRegionEntry` (`malformed control-flow region: errors.join('; ')`) carry the longer text through unchanged. Nothing breaks.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/28055-multi-exit-region-prescribes-join.md`: `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` as sibling lines; the PR body repeats both (`Clause-②: no — refusal text only.` reads as value `no` with trailing reasoning under `clause2-line.mjs`, no arm). Against `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`: a declared `none` must grade every introduced entry `patch` (the one entry is) and may not move an `authorable-surface/` or `authorable-defaults/` baseline (none is in the diff); no `major`. Against `scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs`: the frontmatter is non-empty and no base changeset is modified or deleted. The `Check Changeset` check-run on this head is `success`. Only `@objectstack/spec` source moves (service-automation and lint consume it through the fixed group), so one patch entry is the right level and set. Consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: none declared. Nothing in the diff calls for one.
- `out_of_scope_findings` (carrier none): region traversal has no AND-join, so a node reached by two unconditional paths runs once per arriving path. Read in `traverseNext` (`dag-traversal.ts`): unconditional out-edges fan out as a bucket, conditional ones run one successor. The sentence names an inert node and does not claim run-once, so it is correct for a decision split and for a fork alike; agree with recording it and not filing (no wrong answer at a public door, p3 lineage).
- The cure contains a literal `; ` (`…only exit; an assignment node…`), which is also the separator `validateControlFlow`, `findRegionEntry` and `bpmn-mapping` use between several region errors. No reader splits a region refusal on it today (finding ① 7), so this is a note for any future parser, not a defect.
- The dev's probe transcript lists `ran=["d","x","y"]` without the join `j`; the probe was one-off and is not in the tree, and the committed control (`the join it prescribes is accepted`) pins the registration door the card names, so nothing in this record rests on that line.
- PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (relay `pr_create`), so no second author to name. PR is a draft; `skills/**` untouched, so Tier S, no Tier H approval.
- Check-runs at the time of this read: `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check PR Size` are `success`; Build, Lint, Type Check and Test Core shards were still `in_progress`. The landing precheck (all check-runs green, read from the API) remains the seat's at landing time.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/automation/control-flow.zod.ts` against ADR-0031 and ruling `6521001083`: ADR-0031 fixes regions as single-entry/single-exit sub-graphs owned by `loop`, `parallel` and `try_catch`, with the parallel block's join implicit at block end. The change keeps every word of that: the refusal still fires, and only says how to reach the accepted shape. The docblock on `multiExitRefusal` states why the sentence declines to accept multi-exit and why `assignment` is the node it names, so a later reader does not reopen the question. Against the first consumer, HotCRM's `_guarded-iteration.ts`: the bare `assignment` node is exactly the shape HotCRM already verified against the pinned engine (`config` optional, executor succeeds with no config), so an author following the sentence lands on a tested shape rather than a new one. Against the four axes: a real, measured need (HotCRM found the join by trial, hotcrm#2371); contract-first with no workaround and no semantics change; the prescription names a concrete node kind and the exact edges, which is what an AI author can act on without guessing; no new gate, node kind or accept-set growth. The scenario the card is accepted against (the probe flow `d → x`, `d → y` in a `try_catch` try region, plus a `loop` body and a `parallel` branch) is pinned at the same `where` path, a three-exit case names every exit, and the zero-exit control shows the cure attaches only to the multi-exit line. Holds.
